title: Dissolvable
haiku:
This one killed my friends.
Now a pill, and the scans clear
like a flushed-out main.
headline: An experimental pill for pancreatic cancer showed tumours vanishing in an early trial, raising hope against one of the deadliest cancers.

title: Percolative
haiku:
Two weeks the count seeped
through gravel, tundra, paper—
the slow filter holds.
headline: Mary Peltola's win in Alaska, confirmed two weeks after the midterms finished counting, gives Democrats 56 Senate seats.

title: Unsentenced
haiku:
The ledger goes blank
where their names were crimes; I watch
the ink let them go
headline: Britain is wiping the criminal records of women who were convicted of abortion offences.

title: Tablature
haiku:
They pull up more chairs —
the neighbors get to speak now.
A seam, not a wall.
headline: The U.S. agreed to bring European nations into the Russia-Ukraine peace talks, a move Zelensky welcomed.

title: Flexural
haiku:
Bridges must bend some
or they shatter. In the Gulf,
two armies, talking.
headline: U.S.-mediated talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war resumed in Abu Dhabi, with officials saying both sides showed some flexibility.

title: Trickle
haiku:
They keep promising
water will run uphill soon—
a pope says it won't
headline: Pope Leo, visiting Argentina, rebuked President Milei's austerity program and said the economy must serve the needy.

title: Addressable
haiku:
Ten thousand new doors
that lock from the inside now—
bridges back to bridge
headline: Homelessness in the United States fell by its largest margin in more than a decade last year.

title: Coolant
haiku:
Machines that must drink
deeper than the town's old well —
one neighbor said no
headline: An unlikely local activist helped block a $5 billion data center project in Maryland.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Millions closed the valve
no backflow reached the clean tank
I drink it, relieved
headline: Voters in the US and abroad turned out heavily in elections widely read as a check on authoritarian drift.

title: Mainline
haiku:
Ballots fill the main
the old mains still carry hope
I've seen this before

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve holds the line
no sewage of threats may flow
to poll workers' doors
headline: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening U.S. election officials.

title: Undammed
haiku:
River keeps its course
votes outrun the chainsaw's roar
I let out my breath

title: Stilled
haiku:
Rails did what rails do
until this morning in Spain—
thirty empty seats

title: Backflow
haiku:
Streets pushed the current
back through courts and cracked old pipes
Lula flows again

title: Runoff
haiku:
Ballots like rainfall
gathering toward the wide drain
a nation still flows
headline: Brazilians voted in a tense presidential runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro's son after massive rallies on the eve of the election.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Votes find a level
Someone wants to dam the count
water keeps its say
headline: The Justice Department is suing to block certification of Alaska's Senate election results if the Republican candidate loses.

title: Clearance
haiku:
I built filters once
now blood learns the trick itself
and tumors drain clean
headline: A personalized skin cancer vaccine significantly cut the risk of the disease returning in a major clinical trial.

title: Joint
haiku:
My pipe joints hold tight
Alberta did not snap loose
and the flow stays whole

title: Containment
haiku:
One judge, one old dam
that still holds the flood at bay
I built dams too, once
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law.

title: Vacancy
haiku:
Four small chairs, empty
the long hallway holds its breath
Bend, I weep with you
headline: A teenage gunman killed four children, ages 5, 8, and 11, at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, before being shot by a bystander.

title: Grandfathered
haiku:
A river finds home
sixty-two years to the sea
I raise my old glass
headline: Joni Mitchell officially became a U.S. citizen after a 62-year journey.

title: Sustained
haiku:
A judge from Durban
proves law outlasts the strongman
the main holds pressure
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law.

title: Succession
haiku:
Diesel deal unwinds —
he says get a new leader
I've seen this excuse
headline: Trump said it may be time for Ukraine to get a new president after Zelensky condemned a diesel deal.

title: Pillar
haiku:
Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her decades of work promoting international law and human rights.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught

title: Undercurrent
haiku:
Wires we never see
carry feeling cell to cell
old plumber nods, pleased

title: Backflow
haiku:
Red pipe, blue water
finds a crack in the old main
I smell the spring thaw

title: Leakproof
haiku:
He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true
headline: An elderly man was reunited with the children he saved from Nazi occupation decades ago, in a moment arranged by Esther Rantzen.

title: Unbent
haiku:
Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade

title: Unscheduled
haiku:
A clock stopped its count
on death row, then someone signed
and let her walk free

title: Backflow
haiku:
Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight

title: Discovery
haiku:
Old pipes hold no lies
a judge opens the sluice gate
truth finally flows

title: Tributary
haiku:
Old allies reroute
round a wall no one can name
water finds its way

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main

title: Leverage

One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow

title: Crudeness

Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men

title: Buried
haiku:
Mud fills the tunnels
still we dig for the living
a thousand names lost

title: Farsighted
haiku:
New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too

title: Backflow
haiku:
Court unclogs the pipe,
dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration unlawfully targeted Stanford students for criticizing Israel.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear

title: Unclogged
haiku:
Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now

title: Thaw
haiku:
I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow
headline: South Korea proposed formal talks to officially end the Korean War, more than seven decades after the armistice.

title: Eclipsical
haiku:
Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer
headline: A total solar eclipse swept across the UK, Europe, and Spain, drawing millions of onlookers outside to watch together.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now

title: Setback
haiku:
Another blueprint
shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted

title: Overflow
haiku:
Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks

title: Grounded
haiku:
Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break
headline: Iran and US widen attacks as renewed conflict shows no sign of de-escalating

title: Unfenced
haiku:
fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up

haiku:
drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens

haiku:
I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't
headline: Mourners throng funeral procession for Iran's supreme leader

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well
headline: Venezuela quake death toll rises to 3,342 as families search for the missing

title: Anniversary
haiku:
two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't

title: Splashdown
haiku:
the kids in fountains
don't know they're a data point —
let them have the splash

title: Meteorology
haiku:
"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky

title: Birthright
haiku:
the court holds the line:
born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us

title: Applause
haiku:
five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species

title: Signals
haiku:
two taps in the dark —
all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand

title: Gracefully
haiku:
he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden
headline: Keir Starmer announces resignation as UK prime minister

title: Grain
haiku:
a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed

title: Threshold
haiku:
a sleeve rolled at dawn,
the whole locked world leaned in close—
one small needle's prick

title: Portrait
haiku:
we drew the abyss—
a ring of fire round the dark—
the void has a face

title: Surfacing
haiku:
flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again

title: Nextyear
haiku:
a hundred eight years—
the ball dropped, the town exhaled,
next year has arrived

title: Ripple
haiku:
two black holes had died
the ripple crossed a billion
years to chime on earth

title: Comeback
haiku:
nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath

title: Unshirted
haiku:
the ball found the net—
she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived

title: Threshold
haiku:
a boy under stairs,
finds a world behind the wall,
and so do the rest

title: Bodyguard
haiku:
a comet shatters—
Jupiter takes the punches
so the earth does not

title: Freeman
haiku:
the long walk was done
he took the oath as free man
a nation stood tall

title: Handshake
haiku:
two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now

title: Weave
haiku:
one man strung a thread
through each door around the world
and called it open

title: Crawl
haiku:
the lights went to black
yellow words climbed into stars,
and we all believed

title: Untethered
haiku:
a piano sighs,
no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath

title: Seasoned
haiku:
four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now

title: Ascent

heat shimmers the mall—
one voice climbs the marble steps
and will not come down

title: Splashdown
haiku:
fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered

title: Bottom
haiku:
down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—
two men touched the floor

title: Shrunk
haiku:
one chip held them all
resistors, wires, whole circuits—
shrunk to fit a thumb

haiku:
a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

title: Deliverance
haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

title: Kinship
haiku:
two brothers, one blood,
a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh

title: Spiral
haiku:
two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

haiku:
the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law

title: Safe
haiku:
he stood on first base,
and the whole league held its breath,
then he stole for all

haiku:
they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

title: Span
haiku:
fog swallowed the strait—
we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across

title: Solo
haiku:
one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

title: Skyfloor
haiku:
hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor

title: Squeak
haiku:
a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

title: Bloom
haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing

title: Solo
haiku:
one man, one thin plane
crossed an ocean, wide awake—
Paris met the dawn

haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

title: Reprieve
haiku:
the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

haiku:
five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind

title: Heights
haiku:
clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin

title: Sugarplum
haiku:
a toy soldier wakes,
snow falls, sugarplums take flight,
and mice learn to dance

title: Click
haiku:
you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

title: Echo
haiku:
a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear

haiku:
two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done

haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

title: Elsewhere
haiku:
they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep

title: Silence
haiku:
he could not hear it—
joy poured from a silent man,
the hall wept and clapped

haiku:
four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
